vacation_compare_notes: [Spring Training counts] Section 1 - MLB + NFL: longest run across the four years is 11 days; a 1-week trip is available in 4/4 years, 2 weeks in 0/4, 3 weeks in 0/4.
[Spring Training counts] Section 2 - Section 1 + Stanford/Cal football: longest run across the four years is 11 days; a 1-week trip is available in 4/4 years, 2 weeks in 0/4, 3 weeks in 0/4.
[Spring Training counts] Section 3 - Section 2 + Earthquakes MLS: longest run across the four years is 11 days; a 1-week trip is available in 4/4 years, 2 weeks in 0/4, 3 weeks in 0/4.

[Spring Training counts] All three sections give the same longest run (11 days). Section 1 already saturates the calendar: the MLB season frame plus the NFL season span leave exactly one open corridor a year, so adding Stanford/Cal football or the Earthquakes cannot shorten it further in this reading.

[regular season + postseason only] Section 1 - MLB + NFL: longest run across the four years is 44 days; a 1-week trip is available in 4/4 years, 2 weeks in 4/4, 3 weeks in 4/4. 3-week years: 2026, 2027, 2028, 2029.

[regular season + postseason only] Section 2 - Section 1 + Stanford/Cal football: longest run across the four years is 44 days; a 1-week trip is available in 4/4 years, 2 weeks in 4/4, 3 weeks in 4/4. 3-week years: 2026, 2027, 2028, 2029.
[regular season + postseason only] Section 3 - Section 2 + Earthquakes MLS: longest run across the four years is 12 days; a 1-week trip is available in 4/4 years, 2 weeks in 0/4, 3 weeks in 0/4.
[regular season + postseason only] The sections do NOT agree (Section 1 44 d, Section 2 44 d, Section 3 12 d). Section 3 is the binding constraint.

Sections 1 and 2 always have the same longest run (2026, 2027, 2028, 2029, both readings). Bay Area college football changes only the early-January bowl window, which is conditional on Stanford or Cal qualifying and never creates or destroys a 1-, 2- or 3-week window. Practically: adding Stanford and Cal costs you nothing.

Adding the San Jose Earthquakes is the only change that costs a whole trip - 2026 (regular): 44 d -> 12 d; 2027 (regular): 38 d -> 12 d; 2028 (regular): 40 d -> 12 d; 2029 (regular): 41 d -> 12 d. MLS plays on weekends from late February, and every 7-day window contains a weekend, so no multi-week window can exist inside the MLS season. If you want 2-3 weeks away, Section 3 cannot give it to you; Sections 1 and 2 can.

The reading of 'no MLB games' matters more than the section does. If Spring Training counts, the best week in any year is the 8-11 days between the conference championships and the Pro Bowl, and no section reaches two weeks. If only the regular season and postseason count, Sections 1 and 2 open a 5-6 week corridor from the day after the Super Bowl to Opening Day, and only Section 3 misses out.

Everything the site computes - the day board, the free windows, and the vacation analysis - is computed once per section so the three can be compared side by side.

_meta.why_not_every_nfl_game: The request lists only the San Francisco 49ers plus the Westwood One national feed for the NFL. Those two tags cover roughly five NFL dates a week (Sunday, plus the midweek national window), not all 272 games. The vacation analysis therefore ALSO blocks the NFL league calendar (Hall of Fame Game through the end of the season) as a conservative backstop - see scripts/analyze_vacation.py.
